samples.summary: Theme toggle now blows away the preview DOM for every notes user, not just ones with diagrams
samples.evidence: `setTheme` now unconditionally calls `preview.setTheme(mode)` + `renderPreview()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:440-443), and `NotePreview.render()` does `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:198). The out-of-diff consumer is `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:112`, whose `useEffect([resolvedTheme])` calls `editorRef.current?.setTheme(...)` on every light/dark toggle. Previously a theme switch only reconfigured the CodeMirror theme compartment and left the preview pane untouched; now every toggle wipes the preview's innerHTML, which resets the preview's scrollTop to 0, destroys any text selection the user had made in the preview, and fires a `scroll` event on `preview.el` that the scroll-sync listener registered at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:428 will propagate back into the editor scroller (`linkScroll(preview.el, editorScroller)`), yanking the source pane's scroll position too. This regression hits all notes, including ones with no mermaid fence, which is the only case the repaint exists for.

samples.summary: Mermaid engine/cache state is module-global and shared by every NotePreview; nothing in `dispose()` releases it or stops an in-flight pass
samples.evidence: `renderCache`, `loaded`, `initializedTheme` and `passChain` are module-level singletons (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:90-171). The out-of-diff consumer that owns lifecycle is `initialize()`'s `dispose()` at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:481-487, which tears down listeners and `view.destroy()` but knows nothing about mermaid: a pass already awaiting `load()`/`mermaid.render()` keeps running after the note route unmounts (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:103 calls `editor.dispose()` on unmount), continues to occupy the single global `passChain`, and retains up to 40 SVG strings in `renderCache` for the lifetime of the SPA session. `passSeq` is keyed per root, so an unmounted root's pass is never marked superseded — only the `root.contains(el)` check stops it from painting. A second concurrently-mounted preview (e.g. dev/HMR double-mount or a future split view) also serialises behind the same chain and shares `initializedTheme`.

samples.summary: mermaid pulls Node-only transitive deps (@iconify/utils → @antfu/install-pkg / import-meta-resolve) into the browser bundle; the branch's own verification only exercised diagram types that do not reach them
samples.evidence: pnpm-lock.yaml now records `@iconify/utils@3.1.4` → `@antfu/install-pkg@1.1.0` (tinyexec/child_process) and `import-meta-resolve@4.2.0` (node:fs/node:url) as transitive deps of mermaid@11.16.0. The frontend aliases `@wafflebase/notes` to source (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:229), so these enter the browser build graph; the only Node shims that config installs are for `util` and `assert` (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:232-233, 248-254). docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-todo.md:97-99 claims this 'settles the disputed blast-radius finding' on the grounds that flowchart and sequenceDiagram rendered — but those are not the diagram types that consume @iconify/utils; `architecture-beta` is. A note containing an architecture diagram would be the first path to touch the iconify loader. Impact is bounded by the per-diagram try/catch (mermaid.ts:376), which would surface it as a 'Diagram error' label rather than a crash. Confirming needs a build/render of an `architecture-beta` fence.

samples.summary: Cached SVG reuse injects duplicate element ids when the same fence appears twice in one note
samples.evidence: `renderCache` is keyed on `${theme} ${source}` and the cached markup is applied verbatim to every matching placeholder (`collectPending` → `apply`, packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:232-246 and 355-370). Mermaid bakes the `id` passed to `render()` into the emitted `<svg id=…>` and into its internal marker/gradient/clipPath ids, and `sanitizeSvgMarkup` preserves them (it only strips scripts, `on*`, unsafe URL attrs and CSS refs). Two identical ```mermaid fences in the same note — a realistic case when a user duplicates a block — therefore land two subtrees with the same element ids in the live preview document; SVG `url(#…)` references (arrowheads, gradients) resolve to the first occurrence, so the second diagram can render without its markers. The renderer that consumes this is NotePreview.render() at packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:198.

samples.summary: The notes package's own library build (es + cjs, mermaid not externalised) is likely broken by the new dependency, and no CI lane would tell you
samples.evidence: packages/notes/package.json:38 defines `build: vite --config vite.build.ts build`, and packages/notes/vite.build.ts:19-22 externalises only `@yorkie-js/sdk` while emitting both `es` and `cjs` formats. mermaid and much of its graph (`marked`, `es-toolkit`, `lodash-es`, `@mermaid-js/parser`) are ESM-only, so the CJS half of that lib build would now try to bundle ~3 MB of ESM into `dist/wafflebase-notes.cjs` (the artefact `main` points at, packages/notes/package.json:11). Nothing invokes it: the root `build` script (package.json:8) omits notes and no workflow under .github references it, so this only bites whoever next runs `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/notes build` or publishes dist. Cited here because the diff added the dependency without touching `external` in vite.build.ts.
